about: The Lauda Sion sequence of Saint Thomas Aquinas. It praises Christ present in the Eucharist, expounds transubstantiation, and ends by asking for a share in the banquet of the saints.

seg.tr: Praise, O Sion, thy Savior; praise thy Leader and Shepherd in hymns and canticles.
As much as thou canst, so much dare; for He is greater than all praise, nor canst thou praise Him enough.
A special theme of praise, the living and life-giving Bread, is set forth today.
At the table of the holy supper He was given to the company of the twelve brethren; this is not doubted.
Let praise be full and sounding; let the rejoicing of the mind be glad and fitting.
For a solemn day is kept, on which the first institution of this table is recalled.
At this table of the new King, the new Pasch of the new law brings the ancient Passover to an end.
Newness drives away the old, truth drives away the shadow, and light banishes night.
What Christ did at the supper He commanded to be done in remembrance of Himself.
Taught by sacred precepts, we consecrate bread and wine into the victim of salvation.
A dogma is given to Christians: bread is changed into Flesh, and wine into Blood.
What thou dost not comprehend or see, a courageous faith confirms beyond the ordinary course of nature.
Beneath diverse species, signs only and not realities, excellent realities lie hidden.
The Flesh is food and the Blood is drink; yet Christ remains whole beneath either species.
He is not cut, broken, or divided by the receiver; He is received whole.
One receives, a thousand receive; they receive as much as he, and the One received is not consumed.
The good receive and the wicked receive, yet with unequal lot: of life or of destruction.
It is death to the wicked and life to the good; see how unlike is the outcome of an equal reception.
When at last the Sacrament is broken, waver not, but remember: as much lies beneath the fragment as is covered by the whole.
No division is made in the reality; only the sign is broken, whereby neither the state nor the stature of what is signified is diminished.
Behold the Bread of Angels, made the food of wayfarers; truly the Bread of the children, not to be cast to dogs.
He is foreshadowed in figures: when Isaac is offered, when the paschal lamb is appointed, and when manna is given to the fathers.
Good Shepherd, true Bread, Jesus, have mercy on us. Feed us and guard us; make us behold good things in the land of the living.
Thou who knowest and canst do all things, who feedest us mortals here: make us there Thy table companions, fellow heirs, and comrades of the holy citizens. Amen. Alleluia.
